text.p: Louisiana Pacific Corp, reporting a $0.14 per share loss for the 1996 fourth quarter, said Wednesday it was hurt by unfavorable market conditions, including sharply lower prices for oriented strand board (OSB), and market-related shutdowns.
"Very unfavorable market conditions masked the considerable accomplishments achieved by Louisiana-Pacific in 1996," Mark Suwyn, chairman and chief executive officer, said in a statement.

"We resolved key legal challenges, completely reorganized the company to better serve our customers, added technical capabilities as part of our focus on total quality management, identified three acquisitions to complement our operations, closed a number of underperforming facilities, significantly improved our environmental and safety record, and took major steps toward empowering and training our employee team," he said.
However, near-term prospects continue to be affected by oversupply of OSB, which has dramatically reduced price levels, he said.

"We expect that manufacturers will likely react to this oversupply of OSB by increasing efforts to develop new markets for the product," Suwyn said. "We further expect that high cost, less efficient plants will close, reducing the oversupply situation over time."
In 1996 Louisiana-Pacific closed three of its smaller OSB plants.
